TASK: REVISE ONE SECTION

You wrote section 2 of 6, "What was measured, on whom, and how", of the report "AI readiness of federal statistical publishers: what one measurement shows". It was checked, and it comes back to you once with the notes below. Rewrite the whole section so that the notes no longer apply, keeping its argument and keeping every fact you can keep under the rules.

WHAT THIS SECTION MUST DO: Say what was measured, on which 16 statistical bodies, when, and how: one named composite measurement cycle, one plain identified public client that sent no credentials and never changed its identity, the checks it ran and the findings it holds, how many of the framework's indicators have a rule that measures them, and the literature the framework rests on. Do not report what was found; the next section does.

NOTES
- The phrase (by its content words) 'access policy coherence' occurs 2 times in the report, in sections [1, 2]; say it once and refer back.
- The phrase (by its content words) 'build mark measured' occurs 2 times in the report, in sections [2, 5]; say it once and refer back.
- The phrase (by its content words) 'check access policy' occurs 2 times in the report, in sections [1, 2]; say it once and refer back.
- The phrase (by its content words) 'check discoverability product' occurs 2 times in the report, in sections [1, 2]; say it once and refer back.
- The phrase (by its content words) 'coherence check discoverability' occurs 2 times in the report, in sections [1, 2]; say it once and refer back.
- The phrase (by its content words) 'discoverability product page' occurs 2 times in the report, in sections [1, 2]; say it once and refer back.
- The phrase (by its content words) 'mark measured specify' occurs 2 times in the report, in sections [2, 5]; say it once and refer back.
- The phrase (by its content words) 'policy coherence check' occurs 2 times in the report, in sections [1, 2]; say it once and refer back.

SENTENCES ALREADY CUT (a checker found them unsupported, or a number in them was not in a claim they cite). Do not state these facts again in any wording; the claims do not support them.
- "The framework rests on a corpus of admitted documents that began as a first set of 71 and now holds 282." (checker: The 71 and 282 figures match CL-044, but no claim states that the framework rests on the corpus; that dependency is added by the sentence.)

THE SECTION AS IT STANDS (markers in place)
That framework is put to work in one composite measurement cycle, scan_2026-10-07_composite_d, which is the measurement behind this report and covers 16 statistical bodies [c:CL-050]. Of those bodies, 13 are ranked, because the others have no scored result that rests on a judged finding [c:CL-050]. Across all of them, the cycle judged 24 sets of results and holds 1,055 findings [c:CL-051].

Each of those findings came from a single public client, the scanner, which identified itself by a user agent that names the project and links to its public source [c:CL-034]. Beyond that name the scanner sent nothing, so no credentials, cookies or other identity accompanied any request [c:CL-034]. It also kept the same identity for the whole cycle and never varied it to get a better answer [c:CL-034].

So far, rules measure only part of the framework, because 23 of its 48 indicators have a current rule [c:CL-048]. There are 25 current rules in all, but the rules beyond those 23 indicators belong to the check for access policy coherence and the check for discoverability from the product page, which stay outside the framework count [c:CL-048]. The record's own status marks follow the same line, with 23 of the 48 indicators marked measured, 1 whose measuring tool is built but not yet marked measured, and 24 specified only [c:CL-049].

Of the documents added after that first set, 162 came in before the framework record was first committed and 49 on or after that commit [c:CL-044]. Those 49 later documents are not all literature, however, because 25 of them are captured copies of the scanned web pages rather than published work [c:CL-044].

REGISTER
- Technical and readable. The reader is a federal statistician or a manager at a statistical agency: expert in statistics, not in web crawling or AI.
- Each paragraph carries one thought, stated in its first sentence (the topic sentence); the rest of the paragraph develops it.
- In each sentence, put what the reader already knows first and what is new last, where the stress falls (Gopen and Swan, "The Science of Scientific Writing", 1990).
- Wherever the logic turns (a contrast, a cause, a consequence, an example), say so with a connective word: but, so, because, therefore, for example, however.
- Write whole sentences with a finite verb. Do not follow a long sentence with a short fragment or a short qualifying sentence (for example "Not a browser." or "Only the public pages."); fold the qualification into the sentence it qualifies. This pattern is measured and a section that repeats it fails.
- Vary sentence length naturally. Do not repeat a phrase you have already used; find the plain word for each thing and use it once where once is enough.
- Never use the em dash or the en dash. Never use these words: load-bearing, load bearing, hallucinate (or any form of it; say confabulate), delve, testament. Do not cite Gartner.
- Plain names, no codes. Name a statistical body by its name (the NAMES table gives it), never by a code such as CENSUS or BLS. Name a check by what it tests (for example "the check for a machine-readable licence"), never by a letter-and-number code such as D1 or B2. Do not use task codes, decision numbers, file names, file paths, field names in backticks, or words like harness, pipeline, record node, leg, route, cycle id; call the measuring client "the scanner". The one identifier you may write is the name of the measurement cycle, scan_2026-10-07_composite_d, at most once in the whole report, where the section says what was measured.
- Do not use Markdown formatting inside sentences: no bold, no italics, no backticks, no bullet lists.

FACTS
- Every fact you state must come from the CLAIMS below. Do not use anything you know from elsewhere, even if you are sure it is true. FRAMING text, if any, tells you what the work is for; it is not a source of facts, and a fact taken from it that no claim states will be cut.
- A sentence that states a fact ends with the ids of the claims that support every part of it, written as [c:CL-035] or [c:CL-035, CL-036], placed before the final full stop. A sentence with no fact in it (a transition, a statement of what the section does) has no marker.
- Write every number exactly as a claim states it, in digits, with its thousands separator (1,055, not 1055 or one thousand and fifty-five). Do not compute a new number (no sums, differences, percentages or ratios that no claim states). A number that is not in a claim the sentence cites will be cut.
- Do not overstate. A claim that says "at most", "a bound, not a value", "notional", "not established" or "candidate" keeps that qualification in your sentence.
- A sentence that the claims do not support will be cut, not repaired, and the argument will have a hole where it was.

Return ONLY a JSON object, with no prose before or after it and no code fence:
{"paragraphs": [["first sentence of paragraph one [c:CL-001].", "second sentence."], ["first sentence of paragraph two."]]}
Each paragraph is a list of its sentences, in order; each sentence is one string.

NAMES (a code in a claim, and the name to write instead)
A12: the check for access policy coherence (An identified, robots-compliant machine client that robots.txt permits is served (not refused by a WAF or bot manager))
A13: the check for discoverability from the product page (A machine client starting from the product page reaches the body's API, its terms, its changelog and its inventory without being told where they are)
